text:
alex: Heads-up — customer support ticket #7892: multiple customers reporting a sharp spike in 5xx (502/504) and timeouts to the hosted inference API since today's staged rollout. Hit at ~08:10 UTC.

maya: Which rollout? config flag or new service?

alex: Config flag. We flipped `auth.cache.v2_ttl` in the routing layer during the canary ramp (was supposed to be behind a gate). Canary at 20% when errors started.

raj: Can you paste error snippets from the gateway?

alex: Logs: 
```
[08:13:21] gateway us-west-2 - upstream_error: connection_reset_by_peer -> 502
[08:13:22] gateway us-west-2 - upstream_timeout waiting for auth-service -> 504
[08:13:23] inference-proxy - downstream: 504, q=auth-call, lat=1203ms
```

lin: Region spread? just us-west?

alex: Majority in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Latency and 5xx correlate with auth-service CPU and connection churn.

irene: Support ticket notes say users see repeated client retries that time out. Do we have a reproduced curl?

alex: Repro: `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwoodai.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` -> sometimes 502, sometimes 504 after ~1s.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: staged-rollout/auth-ttl-v2 -> canary 20% -> ramp to 20% at 08:00 UTC

maya: Hypothesis: auth cache TTL mismatch between edge router and auth service causing token revalidation storm. If router TTL shorter, many tokens are refetched/validated simultaneously and auth-service gets overloaded -> upstream timeouts.

raj: Agreed. Also saw `connection_reset_by_peer` which matches overloaded auth workers hitting ulimits.

alex: Immediate ask: roll the flag back to previous value and scale auth-service by +50% for the next 30m. Who can flip the flag?

lin: I can flip now. Command: `./flagctl set auth.cache.v2_ttl 60 --env=prod` (current was 5).

irene: I'll raise replicas: `kubectl scale deploy auth-service -n prod --replicas=8` (was 5).

ops-bot: Executing rollout rollback: `./flagctl set auth.cache.v2_ttl 60` by lin @ 08:17 UTC

alex: After rollback and scale — monitor 5xx across regions and customer ticket. If rates drop, we can replay with staggered canary and synthetic load test.

maya: Also add temporary circuit-breaker on router auth calls to fail fast instead of piling up. Patch: `router.config.auth.max_inflight=200`

raj: Noted — I'll add an alert for auth queue length and connection resets.

support-bot: Support update posted to ticket #7892: "We have identified a config rollout causing upstream auth churn. Rolling back and scaling; ETA 15 min. Temporary mitigation applied."

irene: 08:24 UTC — replicas scaled to 8.

alex: 08:28 UTC — preliminary metrics: 5xx rate down ~70% in us-west-2. Connection resets decreased.

maya: Good. Next steps: postmortem to cover release gating (ensure TTL changes require functional canary that simulates token refresh), add synthetic canary that exercises auth refresh path, and document rollback runbook.

lin: I'll follow up with a short PR to require a rollout safety test for any auth.* flags.

irene: I'll keep customer updated and close the high-priority page when all good.

alex: Thanks team. Pushing incident label and will open a postmortem. :white_check_mark:
